summary: An 80-foot Aeromotor LS40 tower first erected in 1934 at Gilbert Lake, moved to Leonard Hill in 1948, out of regular use after 1988, and closed to the public since.

facts.design: 80-foot Aeromotor LS40 steel fire lookout tower, moved from Gilbert Lake State Park in 1948
facts.status_note: Still on the summit but closed; bottom two sets of stairs removed and cab floor lost to a vandal-set fire, per the 2017 visit

access.note: Closed to the public; the register says so, and Wikipedia says DEC officially closed it in early 1989

visit.trail_note: Closed to the public; the bottom stairs were removed to prevent climbing

facts.agency: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation

events.note: Original erection at Gilbert Lake State Park per NHLR; Wikipedia says the tower stood there from 1932
Moved to Leonard Hill (NHLR); Wikipedia says the Conservation Commission built an 80-foot steel tower on the mountain in 1948; NHLR's Built field also gives 1948
Fire watching ended at the end of the 1988 season
Officially closed by NYS DEC in early 1989
April 23, 2017 visit: bottom stairs removed, cab floor lost to a vandal-set fire, paint and wood need work

corrections.proposed: 1934 built at Gilbert Lake State Park; relocated to Leonard Hill in 1948
corrections.why: The NHLR description says the tower was originally constructed in 1934 at Gilbert Lake and moved in 1948; the brief's 1948 comes from the Built field. Wikipedia gives 1932 for the Gilbert Lake period.

evidence.supports: 80-foot Aeromotor LS40, built 1934 at Gilbert Lake, moved 1948, in operation until 1988, closed to the public
evidence.quote: The 80-foot Aeromotor LS40 fire tower on Leonard Hill was originally constructed in 1934 in Gilbert Lake State Par in Oneonta County. It was moved to its current location in 1948 were it was in operation until 1988. The fire tower is currently closed to the public.
This tower has not been regularly staffed since 1988.

evidence.supports: bottom stairs removed to prevent climbing; cab floor lost to a fire set by vandals
evidence.quote: The bottom two sets of stairs have been removed to prevent climbing and possible injury.

evidence.supports: cab floor lost to a fire set by vandals
evidence.quote: The cab floor is gone to due a fire set by vandals some time ago
New York State Department of Environmental Conservation

evidence.quote: In 1948, the Conservation Commission built an 80-foot-tall (24 m) steel fire lookout tower on the mountain.

evidence.supports: tower stood at Gilbert Lake from 1932 until moved
evidence.quote: The tower was previously standing at Gilbert Lake State Park from 1932 until it was dismantled and moved.

evidence.quote: The tower ceased fire watching operations at the end of the 1988 season and was officially closed in early 1989.
In early 1989, the tower was officially closed by the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation.

evidence.supports: remains on the summit but closed to the public
evidence.quote: The tower remains on the summit, but is closed to the public.

evidence.supports: closed to the public for many years
evidence.quote: the Leonard Hill Fire Tower has been closed to the public for many years now

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says the tower was constructed in 1934 at Gilbert Lake; Wikipedia says it stood there from 1932. Not resolved; the story notes both.
NHLR says Oneonta County, which looks like an error. No source read names the correct county, so the record was not changed on this point.

notes_for_editor: Dates conflict: NHLR 1934 at Gilbert Lake, Wikipedia 1932, and the NHLR Built field 1948. Current status rests on the April 2017 NHLR visit and an undated Gilboa article; no source after 2017 was read. The Gilboa 'tallest tower' claim is unverified. A Daily Star article that might add closure detail returned HTTP 429 and was not read. The page-read budget was exceeded by one (a second Wikipedia fetch).
